items.t: Kremlin declines comment on reports 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war
items.m: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on Wednesday declined to comment on reports in Russian and international news outlets that around 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the Ukraine war so far. The reports were based on hacked data from Russia's official statistics agency. Peskov said only the defence ministry can disclose figures and told reporters "not to pay attention to any other data".

items.t: Moldova issues emergency kit guide, prepares citizens for possible expansion of Ukraine war
items.m: As the war in Ukraine has highlighted the importance of civilian preparedness, Moldova has launched its own emergency readiness programme. Medicine, batteries and three days' worth of food are among the essentials citizens are encouraged to keep at hand, in case they need to leave at a moment's notice.

items.t: 'Paper Tiger': Scarlett Johansson and Adam Driver shine in Russian mob thriller
items.m: This week on arts24, Emma Jones and Dheepthika Laurent discuss the latest film releases. We start with "Paper Tiger", a Russian mob thriller starring Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson and Miles Teller. It is a return to familiar crime thriller territory for James Gray, the director behind "Little Odessa" and "The Yards".

items.t: More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in Ukraine — more than the U.S. lost in World War II or the number of boys born in Russia in a single year
items.m: Over nearly five years of the full-scale war with Ukraine, at least 700,000 Russian troops have died. That estimate comes from journalists at Meduza and Mediazona, based on an analysis of data from a hacked Rosstat database and other sources. After the story was published, many people tried to grasp the scale of these losses by comparing them to the aftermath of other wars and disasters. Here is the list we came up with.

items.t: Russian government official warns of Ukrainian drone attacks on utility infrastructure this winter
items.m: MOSCOW, Nov 25 - Preparations for potential Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian utility infrastructure this winter, particularly in regions near the border, are a top priority for the government, Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin said on Wednesday.

items.t: Moldova launches national preparedness campaign after drone incursions

The “Moldova Ready” campaign, launched in Chisinau, includes a display of the remains of a drone carrying 52kg of explosives after it crashed in the country last month. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.

items.t: Russian casualties in Ukraine war: New reports suggest death toll as high as 700,000
items.m: New analysis of leaked Russian government data suggests some 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the war against Ukraine. Independent Russian media outlets have updated their estimates of Moscow's military casualties after Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers obtained figures from the Russian statistics agency.

items.t: Why Howard Buffett committed $1.33 billion to Ukraine and offered $14 million for a $1 million request
items.m: Warren Buffett’s son Howard Buffett has committed $1.33 billion to Ukraine through his foundation and visited the country 27 times since the war began. His philanthropy includes a striking $14 million contribution to a rehabilitation centre after its team initially sought just $1 million, along with support for food, infrastructure, agriculture and demining efforts.
